metadata.title: Two Applications of Topological Fixed Point Theory

nodes.name: Pencil of Geodesics
nodes.statement: A \textit{pencil} of geodesics is a (non-intersecting) family of geodesics any two of which lie within a finite Hausdorff distance of one another.
nodes.statement_clean: A non-intersecting family of geodesics, pairwise within finite Hausdorff distance.

nodes.name: Gromov Compactification
nodes.statement: For a Cartan-Hadamard manifold $M$, the Gromov compactification is $\bar{M} := M \cup M(\infty)$, where $M(\infty)$ is the ideal boundary; $\bar{M}$ is homeomorphic to the closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n} \subset \mathbb{R}^{n}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Compactification of M by adding the ideal boundary, yielding a closed ball.

nodes.name: Connectivity of a Planar Domain
nodes.statement: The connectivity of a bounded planar domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}$ counts the number of boundary components; here $\Omega_{k}$ has connectivity $k+1$ with boundary consisting of finitely many smooth Jordan curves.
nodes.statement_clean: Number of boundary components of a planar domain.

nodes.name: Generalised Lefschetz Number
nodes.statement: The generalised Lefschetz number $\lambda(\sigma)$ extends the classical Lefschetz number to non-compact Lefschetz spaces; for fixed-point-free maps it vanishes.
nodes.statement_clean: Lefschetz number generalized to certain non-compact spaces.

nodes.name: Cartan's Fixed Point Theorem
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold of non-positive curvature. If $\sigma \in Isom(M)$ has finite order, then $Fix(\sigma) \neq \emptyset$.
nodes.statement_clean: Every finite-order isometry of a Cartan-Hadamard manifold has a fixed point.
assumptions: $M$ is a complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold

nodes.name: Pencil of Geodesics Preserved
nodes.statement: Under the hypotheses of Cartan's Theorem, if $\dim M$ is odd, then there exists a pencil $\Gamma$ of geodesics such that $\sigma(\Gamma) = \Gamma$.
nodes.statement_clean: In odd dimension, a finite-order isometry preserves a pencil of geodesics.
conclusions: There exists a pencil $\Gamma$ of geodesics with $\sigma(\Gamma) = \Gamma$

nodes.name: Prime Divisor Constraint for Aut$(\Omega_k)$
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega_{k} \subset \mathbb{C}$ be a bounded planar domain of connectivity $k+1$ ($k \geq 2$) with smooth Jordan boundary. If $p$ is a prime dividing $|Aut(\Omega_{k})|$, then $k^{3} \equiv k \bmod p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Any prime dividing |Aut(Omega_k)| must satisfy k^3 = k mod p.
assumptions: Boundary is finitely many smooth Jordan curves

nodes.name: Cartan-Hadamard Theorem
nodes.statement: A complete, simply connected Riemannian manifold $M$ of non-positive curvature is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{n}$, where $n = \dim M$.
nodes.statement_clean: Cartan-Hadamard manifolds are diffeomorphic to Euclidean space.

nodes.name: Brouwer's Fixed Point Theorem
nodes.statement: Every continuous self-map of the closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}^{n}$ has a fixed point.
nodes.statement_clean: Continuous self-maps of a closed ball admit fixed points.

nodes.name: Mod $p$ Lefschetz Theorem
nodes.statement: If $\bar{\tau}$ is a self-map of a suitable space and $p$ is prime, then $\lambda(\bar{\tau}) \equiv \lambda(\bar{\tau}^{p}) \bmod p$.
nodes.statement_clean: Lefschetz numbers satisfy a congruence under p-th iteration.
assumptions: $\bar{\tau}$ a self-map on the relevant space

nodes.name: Finiteness of Aut$(\Omega_{k})$
nodes.statement: For a bounded planar domain $\Omega_{k}$ with smooth boundary and connectivity $k+1 > 2$, the conformal automorphism group $Aut(\Omega_{k})$ is finite.
nodes.statement_clean: Aut(Omega_k) is finite when connectivity exceeds two.
assumptions: $\Omega_{k}$ bounded planar domain with smooth boundary

nodes.name: Heins' Sharp Upper Bounds
nodes.statement: For $k \geq 2$: $\#Aut(\Omega_{k}) \leq 2k$ for $k \notin \{4,6,8,12,20\}$, and $\#Aut(\Omega_{4}) \leq 12$, $\#Aut(\Omega_{6}), \#Aut(\Omega_{8}) \leq 24$, $\#Aut(\Omega_{12}), \#Aut(\Omega_{20}) \leq 60$.
nodes.statement_clean: Heins' sharp upper bounds for the order of Aut(Omega_k).

nodes.name: Bound on Fixed Points of Conformal Automorphisms
nodes.statement: For an automorphism $\sigma \in Aut(\Omega_{k})$ of prime order, $\#Fix(\sigma) \leq 2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Prime-order conformal automorphisms have at most two fixed points.

nodes.name: Euler Characteristic of a Wedge of Circles
nodes.statement: If $\Omega$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of $(k + \#Fix(\sigma))$ circles, then $\chi(\Omega) = 1 - k - \#Fix(\sigma)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Euler characteristic of a wedge of m circles is 1 - m.
assumptions: $\Omega$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of $(k + \#Fix(\sigma))$ circles

nodes.name: Fix Bound Equation
nodes.statement: $\#Fix(\sigma) \leq 2$.

nodes.name: Lefschetz Vanishing Mod $p$
nodes.statement: $0 = \lambda(\bar{\tau}) \equiv \lambda(\bar{\tau}^{p}) \bmod p$.

nodes.name: Euler Characteristic Congruence
nodes.statement: $\chi(\Omega) = 1 - k - \#Fix(\sigma) \equiv 0 \bmod p$.

nodes.name: Cyclic Group of Order 7 Constraint
nodes.statement: The cyclic group of order $7$ cannot occur as a subgroup of $Aut(\Omega_{k})$ for any $k < 6$, since otherwise $7 \mid (k^{3} - k)$ would fail; the upper bound $\#Aut(\Omega_{5}) \leq 10$ does not exclude this.
nodes.statement_clean: Order-7 cyclic group is not a subgroup of Aut(Omega_k) for k < 6.

nodes.name: Characterising Automorphism Groups of Planar Domains
nodes.statement: It is an open problem to characterise the finite groups which may occur as the automorphism groups of bounded planar domains.

nodes.name: Proof of Cartan's Fixed Point Theorem
nodes.statement: By induction on $\dim M$ using Brouwer's theorem on the Gromov compactification $\bar{M} \approx \mathbb{B}^{n}$ and reduction via horospheres at ideal-boundary fixed points.

nodes.name: Compactify $M$ and lift $\sigma$
nodes.statement: By Cartan-Hadamard, $M$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{n}$; form $\bar{M} = M \cup M(\infty) \approx \mathbb{B}^{n}$, and $\sigma$ extends to a homeomorphism $\bar{\sigma}$ of $\bar{M}$.

nodes.name: Apply Brouwer to $\bar{\sigma}$
nodes.statement: By Brouwer's fixed point theorem, $\bar{\sigma}$ has a fixed point $x \in \bar{M}$.

nodes.name: Inductive descent via horospheres
nodes.statement: If $x \in M(\infty)$, then $\bar{\sigma}$ maps a horosphere centred at $x$ to itself; this horosphere is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{B}^{n-1}$, so the argument repeats with reduced dimension.

nodes.name: Base case: dimension two
nodes.statement: If the inductive descent reaches dimension two with all fixed points on $M(\infty)$, the argument yields a $\sigma$-invariant geodesic $\gamma \subset M$ isometric to $\mathbb{R}$; any finite-order isometry of $\mathbb{R}$ has a fixed point.

nodes.name: Proof of Corollary on Pencil of Geodesics
nodes.statement: By contradiction using the mod $p$ Lefschetz Theorem applied to the action induced by $\bar{\sigma}$ on $\mathbb{R}P^{n-1} = M(\infty)/(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})$.

nodes.name: Pass to projective quotient
nodes.statement: $\bar{\sigma}$ restricts to a homeomorphism of $M(\infty) \approx \mathbb{S}^{n-1}$; quotient by the $\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ action (forgetting direction) yields $\mathbb{R}P^{n-1}$ with an induced action.

nodes.name: Assume no fixed point and pick smallest $m$
nodes.statement: Assume the induced action has no fixed points. Let $m \in \mathbb{N}$ be the smallest power of $\bar{\sigma}$ with $\lambda(\bar{\sigma}^{m}) \neq 0$; since $n-1$ is even, $\lambda(Id_{\mathbb{R}P^{n-1}}) = \chi(\mathbb{R}P^{n-1}) = 1$, so $m$ does not exceed the order of $\bar{\sigma}$.

nodes.name: Apply mod $p$ Lefschetz Theorem
nodes.statement: If $m \neq 1$, pick a prime $p \mid m$ and set $\bar{\tau} = \bar{\sigma}^{m/p}$. Then $0 = \lambda(\bar{\tau}) \equiv \lambda(\bar{\tau}^{p}) \bmod p$.

nodes.name: Derive contradiction $0 \equiv 1 \bmod p$
nodes.statement: We obtain $0 \equiv 1 = \chi(\mathbb{R}P^{n-1}) \bmod p$, a contradiction. Hence the induced action has a fixed point, corresponding to a $\sigma$-invariant pencil $\Gamma$ of geodesics.

nodes.name: Proof of Prime Divisor Constraint Theorem
nodes.statement: Apply the generalised Lefschetz number to the restriction of $\sigma$ to $\Omega = \Omega_{k} \setminus Fix(\sigma)$, which has the homotopy type of a wedge of $(k + \#Fix(\sigma))$ circles.

nodes.name: Pick prime-order $\sigma$ and bound fixed points
nodes.statement: Select an arbitrary $\sigma \in Aut(\Omega_{k})$ of prime order $p$; by Krantz Thm. 1.4.3, $\#Fix(\sigma) \leq 2$.

nodes.name: Pass to non-compact $\Omega$ and use generalised Lefschetz number
nodes.statement: Let $\Omega = \Omega_{k} \setminus Fix(\sigma)$; $\Omega$ is a Lefschetz space (Dugundji-Granas Thm. 4.1, p. 423). The restriction of $\sigma$ to $\Omega$ is fixed-point-free, so its generalised Lefschetz number $\lambda(\sigma)$ vanishes.

nodes.name: Compute Euler characteristic and reduce mod $p$
nodes.statement: Since $\Omega$ has the homotopy type of a wedge of $(k + \#Fix(\sigma))$ circles, $\chi(\Omega) = 1 - k - \#Fix(\sigma) \equiv 0 \bmod p$.

nodes.name: Conclude $p \mid k$ or $p \mid k \pm 1$
nodes.statement: Combined with $\#Fix(\sigma) \leq 2$, the congruence forces $p$ to divide one of $k, k-1, k+1$, i.e. $k^{3} \equiv k \bmod p$.
